clue.text: Person with diamonds on upper part of dress

parts.note: bod is informal British slang for a person or body
ice is slang for diamonds, from their cold glitter

explanation.surface: Someone wearing diamonds on the top half of a gown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'on' only join the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodice is the fitted top section of a woman's dress, above the waist.

clue.text: Drop off at end of storm

explanation.surface: Something falls away at the tail end of a gale.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow over is both to subside or die away, as interest drops off, and what a storm does when it passes and ends.

clue.text: Chief said abroad first it's a narrow channel

indicators.note: first tells us the foreign word for said comes before the abbreviation for chief

parts.note: dit is French for said, so said in a foreign language

explanation.surface: A leader spoke overseas before announcing a narrow waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' sets DIT ahead of CH, against the clue's order of Chief then said; 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A ditch is a long narrow trench dug in the ground, usually for drainage water.

clue.text: Bird in spy organisation found bloomer

indicators.note: in places the bird inside the letters of the spy agency

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency, the spy service
a lark is a songbird

explanation.surface: A bird was discovered within the CIA, which turned out to be a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' reads as a mistake (British slang for a blunder) but is a flower, something that blooms; 'found' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarkia is a genus of North American garden annuals grown for their showy flowers, so it is a plant that blooms.

clue.text: Wager about ailing digs

indicators.note: about means the wager goes around the word for sick

parts.note: a wager is a bet
ailing means sick or ill

explanation.surface: Someone gambles while feeling poorly about where they lodge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digs' is British slang for lodgings, not a verb meaning to excavate.
explanation.definitionFit: A billet is lodging, especially quarters for soldiers in a private house, which is what digs means in British slang.

clue.text: I will go up in command despite having incorrect reasoning

parts.note: I will contracts to I'll

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word go is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: taken as written before being turned
IC is the abbreviation for in charge or in command, as in second-in-command (2IC)

explanation.surface: Someone climbs into a position of authority despite their muddled thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses GO to OG in this down clue; 'despite having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Illogic is a lack of logic, faulty argument or unsound thinking.

clue.text: Flat dweller

parts.note: reads as someone living in an apartment, but means a person who lives on level low-lying land

explanation.definitionFit: Someone from low, level country such as the Scottish Lowlands lives on flat terrain rather than in an apartment.

clue.text: A rum sort in army suffered distressing experience

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters inside the army's abbreviation

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, the British volunteer reserve force

indicators.note: sort means the letters of a rum are rearranged, as when sorting things out

explanation.surface: A strange character in the army went through something awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort' rearranges A RUM into RAUM, which goes 'in' TA; 'A rum sort' reads as an odd fellow. 'suffered' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Trauma is a deeply disturbing or shocking event and the emotional harm it leaves.

clue.text: No way to drive along

parts.note: reads as an exclamation of refusal, but describes a route on which vehicles may not travel, meant for walkers only

explanation.definitionFit: A path for pedestrians is a way where cars cannot be driven.

clue.text: Doubly bitter one?

parts.note: suggests something twice as sour, but means a pint mixing two beers in equal measure, such as bitter with mild

explanation.definitionFit: A mixture of two drinks in equal parts, traditionally ale with stout or bitter with mild, is poured as this in British pubs.

clue.text: Act with fellow sheriff

parts.note: an act of parliament is a law
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A sheriff takes action alongside a companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: In the American West a sheriff was an enforcer of the legal code, a lawman.

clue.text: Stylish post office shut up

parts.note: sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A smart post office has closed.
explanation.definitionFit: Posh means upper-class, smart and elegant.

clue.text: One or two weights? …

parts.note: a single unit of mass equal to a thousand grammes, which also splits into two words that are each units of weight

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into 13 across, which also talks of weight.
explanation.definitionFit: This metric unit is one weight, yet its name joins kilo and gramme, two separate weights.

clue.text: … Of equal weight, that's sensible

explanation.surface: Things balancing evenly are a matter of good sense.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 12 across's weights; 'that's' joins the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes scales or loads evenly poised, and also a person who is sane, stable and level-headed.

clue.text: Register with mirth a problematical mathematical aid

parts.note: a log is a register or record, as in a ship's log

indicators.note: problematical suggests the letters of mirth a are in a troubled, disordered state

explanation.surface: A tricky maths tool records hilarity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problematical' is the anagram signal working on MIRTH A; 'with' is a link, and 'Register' is a noun here, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Tables of these exponent values were long used to turn multiplication into addition, a calculating aid.

clue.text: Made a ruling

parts.note: reads as delivering a judgement, but means exercised rule, controlled a state

explanation.definitionFit: A monarch or government that ruled a country controlled its affairs.

clue.text: One likely to have too much on his plate

definitions.text: One likely to have too much on his plate

parts.words: One likely to have too much on his plate
parts.note: suggests an overworked man with too many tasks, but literally means a glutton piling food high

explanation.definitionFit: A glutton takes more food than needed, so heaps the dinner plate.

clue.text: Open race I had entered

indicators.note: entered says the contraction goes inside the word for a race

parts.note: a race is a sporting event
I had contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: A competitor enters an open race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open' looks like an open race but is the definition, meaning plain to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Open as an adjective means obvious, plain or manifest.

clue.text: Tyne cop's remarkable power

indicators.note: remarkable suggests something out of the ordinary, signalling the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A policeman on Tyneside has impressive strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remarkable' rearranges TYNE COP; the Tyne is a river in north-east England, by Newcastle.
explanation.definitionFit: Potency is strength, force or effectiveness.

clue.text: Former harbour used to send things abroad

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a port is a harbour

explanation.surface: An old harbour was once used for shipping goods overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used to' is a link here, though it reads as part of the past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: To export is to sell goods to a foreign country, shipping them out.

clue.text: Steep tax Breton and I reimposed

indicators.note: reimposed suggests the letters are set out afresh in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Breton and I face a heavy tax being levied again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reimposed' rearranges TAX BRETON I; 'and' only joins the fodder. 'Steep' looks like part of the tax but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Steep in the sense of a price means unreasonably high or excessive.

clue.text: Manner of chaps going round Italy

indicators.note: going round means the chaps surround the letter for Italy

parts.note: chaps are men
I is the international vehicle registration code for Italy

explanation.surface: The bearing of men touring Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Mien is a person's bearing, look or demeanour.

clue.text: Car test or vehicle undergoing it

parts.note: the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for cars in Britain, named after the Ministry of Transport
taken as written

explanation.surface: A car's inspection, or the vehicle being inspected.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers back to the test: the vehicle that undergoes the MOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A car taken in for testing is an automobile, an everyday word for it.

clue.text: Something afoot? Disapprove at driver's place

parts.note: boo is the call made to show disapproval
in golf the driver is a club, used from the tee

explanation.surface: Something is going on; a golfer jeers at the tee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'afoot' usually means happening, but here it means worn on a foot; 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby's knitted woollen shoe is literally on a foot.

clue.text: Make small adjustments to very good piece of music

parts.note: fine means very good, excellent
a tune is a piece of music

explanation.surface: Tweaking things to a lovely melody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjust precisely, as tuning an instrument, is to make tiny corrections for best performance.

clue.text: Thomas to include a fruit

indicators.note: include means the letter a goes inside the run of the two words

parts.note: Tom is the short form of the name Thomas
taken as written

explanation.surface: Thomas brings a piece of fruit with him.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically it is the fleshy seed-bearing part of a plant, a berry, though cooked as a vegetable.

clue.text: Cross part of lengthy bridge

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Crossing part of a long bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross between two breeds or species is the offspring of mixed parentage.
